hints: Notice the feather starts from rest so $u = 0$, and vacuum means no air resistance so acceleration is $g \approx 9.8 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ downwards.
Connect the fall distance to time with $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$, which simplifies to $s = \frac{1}{2}gt^2$ for this drop.
Substitute $t = 0.5 \text{ s}$ and check that $0.5^2 = 0.25$ before multiplying by $\frac{1}{2} \times 9.8$ to estimate the tube length.
walkthrough: Identify the motion: initial velocity $u = 0$, time $t = 0.5 \text{ s}$, and because the tube is evacuated the feather is in free fall with $a = g \approx 9.8 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Select the displacement equation for uniform acceleration: $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$.
Simplify for release from rest: $u = 0$ so $s = \frac{1}{2}gt^2$.
Substitute values with units: $s = 0.5 \times 9.8 \text{ m s}^{-2} \times (0.5 \text{ s})^2$.
Calculate the intermediate result: $(0.5)^2 = 0.25$, so $s = 0.5 \times 9.8 \times 0.25 \text{ m} \approx 1.225 \text{ m}$.
Round to a sensible length close to $1.2 \text{ m}$. This is option A.
